releases.body:
# reverse-skill v1.0.0

**First formal release** — 2026-07-18

AI-powered skill router for authorized reverse engineering, penetration testing, and security research.

## Highlights

| Area | What you get |
|------|----------------|
| **PRIMARY path** | `MASTER-ROUTING.md` + `master-route.ps1` → correct skill in one hop |
| **Ops contracts** | Scope / auth gate, Evidence→Finding→Path, roles, timeline |
| **Case tooling** | `case-init` · `case-guard` · `append-evidence` · `smoke` · `verify-routing-coherence` |
| **Skill matrix** | 20+ modules (APK, IDA, r2, JS, .NET, pwn, firmware, pentest, LLM, …) |
| **Bootstrap** | On-demand toolchain install from `bootstrap-manifest.json` |
| **Knowledge loop** | `field-journal` + docs-generator completion checklist |
| **Platforms** | Windows primary; Linux / macOS / Kali supported paths |

## Install (quick)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill.git
cd reverse-skill
# Windows
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File skills/scripts/refresh-tool-index.ps1
# Linux / macOS
bash skills/scripts/refresh-tool-index.sh
```

Point your AI client at `RULES.md` / `README_AI.md`. See [README.md](../README.md).

## Verif

aiSummary.oneLiner: A comprehensive cybersecurity skill routing package that provides structured playbooks and toolchains for AI coding agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Reverse-skill acts as an operational knowledge base and tool router for AI agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex CLI. When an AI agent encounters a cybersecurity task—such as reverse engineering an APK, analyzing malware, competing in a CTF, or bypassing frontend JavaScript encryption—it provides strict routing rules and scenario-specific playbooks. Instead of letting the AI guess commands, it forces the agent to read operational contracts, check local tool availability (e.g., IDA, Frida, apktool), and execute repeatable, structured workflows. It maintains an evolving field journal to reuse experience across sessions.
keyFeatures: AI playbook routing: Intercepts AI agent workflows to enforce strict methodologies for over 20 cybersecurity scenarios including mobile, binary, and web analysis.
Toolchain bootstrapping: Automatically detects local security tools (like Java, Node.js, Python, and Frida) and generates an index so the AI knows what is available.
Evidence chain enforcement: Requires agents to log findings into a structured timeline and field journal before executing commands, preventing random hacking attempts.
Self-evolving knowledge base: Maintains local case directories and experience logs so the AI doesn't repeat the same mistakes across different sessions.
Multi-platform support: Includes specific configuration scripts and docs for running seamlessly on Kali Linux, standard Debian/Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.

useCases.title: Automated malware analysis
useCases.description: Security researchers point their AI agent at a suspicious binary, and the router automatically selects the IDA/radare2 playbook to extract YARA rules.

useCases.title: Mobile app reverse engineering
useCases.description: Penetration testers use the APK skill route to automatically unpack an Android application, run jadx, and hook TLS encryption via Frida.

useCases.title: CTF competition orchestration
useCases.description: Capture The Flag competitors deploy the sandbox orchestrator to let the AI systematically solve cryptography and binary exploitation challenges.

useCases.title: Frontend encryption bypass
useCases.description: Web scrapers use the JS reverse playbook to automatically analyze and deobfuscate custom Webpack bundles or DSL virtual machines.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This repository is built for penetration testers, reverse engineers, and security researchers who want to augment their workflows using autonomous AI agents guided by strict, professional methodologies.
